questions.prompt: What makes a file a "module" in TypeScript?

options.text: Using top-level import/export; its top-level names are private unless exported

questions.explanation: A file with top-level import/export is a module. Its top-level declarations are scoped to the file unless exported.

options.text: When an imported name is used only as a type — it's always erased and avoids accidental runtime imports

questions.explanation: import type marks a type-only import, guaranteeing it's erased and preventing a needless (or invalid) runtime import under strict module settings.

options.text: A types-only file describing the shape of code implemented elsewhere

questions.explanation: A declaration file contains types only (no implementations). The standard library itself is a set of .d.ts files.

questions.prompt: Types for a library that ships none usually come from a community package under the ______ scope on DefinitelyTyped. (include the @ symbol)
questions.explanation: The @types scope hosts community-maintained type packages that the compiler picks up automatically.

questions.prompt: What does an ambient `declare module 'x' { ... }` do?

options.text: Provides types for a module (often plain JavaScript) that has no type declarations of its own

questions.explanation: An ambient declare module supplies types for an untyped module, so imports from it are type-checked.

questions.prompt: Which `moduleResolution` value is typical for a Vite/webpack app, and which for Node?

options.text: classic for apps; amd for Node
bundler for the app; nodenext for Node.js
node for apps; bundler for Node

questions.explanation: Apps built with bundlers use moduleResolution 'bundler'; Node programs use 'node16'/'nodenext' to match Node's resolution rules.
